errorCodes.meaning: The community owns no room with this identifier.
`member` holds neither an admission to the room nor an open offer.
The community's VTA, or the room's host behind it, did not answer. The outcome is unknown: a removal the VTA may have completed is settled by retrying, which it answers from its own record.
The community's VTA refused the removal. Its own code and message are carried in `details`. Nothing changed.

DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MemberAction.description: What a member of a community-owned room may do there. `admin` is not among them: minting epochs, admitting and removing members are the community's, as the room's owner, and are exercised through the vtc/rooms/community/* tasks rather than by any member's credential. `curate` is not implied by `write`.
MemberAction.title: MemberAction

MemberActions.description: The actions granted, at least one. An empty list confers nothing rather than everything, and a schema that allowed it would make the more dangerous reading available to a careless consumer.
MemberActions.title: MemberActions

MemberState.description: Where an admission stands. `offered`: credentials issued and waiting for the member to collect and accept them. `admitted`: accepted — on a sealed tier, the member is in the room's group. `removed`: an administrator removed them; on a sealed tier the room has advanced past them.
MemberState.title: MemberState

Reason.description: Why the administrator is making this change. Recorded with it in the audit trail. Attributed to its author on every surface and untrusted: it MUST NOT carry personal data or a credential, and a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions.
Reason.title: Reason

Response.description: Success response to vtc/rooms/community/members/remove. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/rooms/community/members/remove/0.2#response. The member as recorded, in state `removed`; on `open` and `attributed` rooms the revocation list in force at the room's host, from which the member's credentials are refused; and on a sealed tier the epoch the room advanced to.

epoch.description: On a sealed tier, the room epoch after the removal.

revocation.description: On an `open` or `attributed` room: the room's revocation list carrying the withdrawal, as the room's host accepted it. From then on the host refuses every credential the room issued the member before `revokedAt`. Absent on a `private` room, where a member cannot be withdrawn one at a time and their credentials are honoured until `member.validUntil`.

Response.title: VTC Rooms Community Members Remove — response payload

RevocationHead.description: Which `RevocationList` a party holds, without its entries: comparable between the room's key holder and a host, and between two hosts, without disclosing whom the room withdrew.

digest.description: SHA-256 multihash of the list's RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, `proof` included. Two parties holding one sequence with different digests have been given two lists the room signed at one sequence.

RevocationHead.title: RevocationHead

RoomMember.description: One party the community admitted to a room it owns, or offered admission to.

validUntil.description: When the member's authority credential expires.

RoomMember.title: RoomMember
